title: Analysis of tumor DNA markers in the plasma of cancer patients by liquid biopsy
summary:
Liquid biopsy is a procedure for examining cell-free tumor DNA in the blood of patients. It is based on the fact that the components of dead body cells, including the genetic material (DNA) of dead tumor cells, are first removed via the blood before they are broken down. A small amount of tumor DNA is therefore usually found in the blood of a patient who still has tumor cells. It is already technically possible to detect individual mutations of the tumor in the blood. This is useful for determining whether tumor cells remain in the body and for detecting changes in the tumor DNA that may have an influence on the success of the ongoing therapy. 
The aim of the current project is to detect tumor markers in very small amounts of ctDNA.  In addition, a new method for the non-targeted identification of tumor markers is to be established in order to expand the range of possible clinical applications for liquid biopsy. To this end, blood serum samples from patients with solid tumors will be examined before the start of treatment and during the course of treatment. As this is a study to establish and validate a new method whose reliability is to be tested and optimised, individual results will not be communicated as part of the project and therefore have no influence on the treatment of patients.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung
